blocks.content: The Reserve Bank of India was established on April 1, 1935 in accordance with the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.

rows: RBI Act, 1934 & RBI (Transfer to Public Ownership) Act, 1948

items: Hilton Young Commission (Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance, 1926) recommended the creation of the central bank.
RBI was nationalised on January 1, 1949, making it fully government-owned.
Section 7 of the RBI Act empowers the Central Government to issue directions to the Bank in the public interest after consultation with the Governor.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Reserve Bank of India was established on April 1, 1935, following the recommendations of the Hilton Young Commission (1926).
Operations commenced under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, with an initial share capital of ₹5 crore divided into shares of ₹100 each.
Initially established as a private shareholders' bank, the RBI was nationalised on January 1, 1949, under the RBI (Transfer to Public Ownership) Act, 1948.
The Central Office was originally set up in Kolkata but was permanently relocated to Mumbai in 1937.
